prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1103; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the policyholder's driver reporting a side impact at a signalized intersection. The claimant states they were struck on the driver's side by a vehicle entering from the cross street, and confirmed that the driver is named on the policy.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed coverage was in force at the time of loss, with no sign of any issue predating the coverage start. Requested the police report, photos from the scene, and statements from the other driver and a witness.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant, who is not represented by an attorney, and took a recorded statement. The account matched the first report in every detail. The claimant reports a back strain from the impact and says they sought care the following day.

Entry 4: Received scene photos and the witness statement. Both support the claimant's description of the collision and the other driver has confirmed the sequence of events. Vehicle damage is concentrated along the driver's side and appears largely consistent with the described impact.

Entry 5: Obtained medical records showing the reported injury is consistent with the type and force of a side impact. Treatment followed a typical course and tapered as the claimant improved. Records show no prior complaints involving the same area of the back.

Entry 6: Reviewed the vehicle inspection. No prior damage to the vehicle is known from the prior claims history. The claimant could not say with certainty which seat position they occupied at the moment of impact, though this does not appear to change the overall picture of the loss.

Entry 7: Reviewed all materials. Injury, vehicle damage, witness accounts, and scene evidence fit together, and the claimant's account has stayed consistent throughout. File moved to the next stage for evaluation of the bodily injury and property damage components.
